d267fc1b: If there is no data in the ^DD global for this field, perform a lookup.  If not doing a LAYGO file, if value is '@', branch.  If field is not read-only and value is '@', branch to input transform.  If value is '@', set to the looked-up value.  Go to standard input processing.
78148c73: Process the X parameter if it is a local array @DQ(DQ,2)
d0e71795: If DG contains P and file X exists, get the record number from ^X(0) and check if the 0 node exists for the DQ array entry. If so, get the value and external value for X and update DG.

55e04229: If DG contains V and Y is a number and formatted like a global reference, get the record number from the 0 node. Check if the Y node exists. If so, get the value. If the DD has a .01 field defined, update DG with the external value and X with the computed value.

f7eddded: Check if the input string contains D. If so, get the specified entry from the data dictionary (DD) file. If the input also contains S, retrieve the piece of the input string after Y: and store it in Y.

3c3b79a2: If the input field is blank, set it to the default edit value for that field (DE). Quit if the input does not pass the data validation (DV) or if the LAYGO value (DC) is less than 2. Otherwise, go to the input transform routine (N^DIE17).
dc27b1aa: If the data validation (DV) does not contain I (input transform) or # (computed expression), go to the reader input (RD).
18a3cd49: Perform the input transform logic (E^DIE0). If the transformed input (X) exists, go to the reader input (RD). Otherwise, go to the prompt (PR).
56833d36: Quit (end of routine).

8a298b09: Set DGJTDDT to the next admission date if it exists, otherwise use the current admission date.

ee294c78: Branch to the appropriate entry points in the DIE17 routine based on the value of Y. If Y is undefined or equal to the delimiter character, go to the 'A' label. Otherwise, set X to Y, set DIC(0) to 'F', set DW to the value of DQ, and go to the OUT^DIE17 label.

7e79a05c: If the input date X is before the event date DGJTDDT, clear the first piece of the 'DT' node in file 393, and write an error message stating that the date must be equal to or after the event date. No time is required. Set Y to '@8', which likely indicates an error condition.
